descriptor: Long reads on design teams and their habits

voice.summary: Halftone Review writes essays, not posts: a reflective voice that reports what a team noticed before telling you what it means. It trusts the reader with nuance and keeps the pace of someone thinking aloud.
dos: Open with a concrete scene or number, then draw the point
Use footnotes for asides instead of cluttering the line
Name what was lost as plainly as what was gained
donts: Avoid listicle headlines and 'ten lessons' framing
Do not claim a result the evidence does not support
Never bury the reader in jargon

taglines: What the dashboard never told us
Essays on how teams really work
boilerplate: Halftone Review is an independent long-form publication examining how design teams work, measure and decide, with reader-friendly typography and room for footnotes.
